title: 2020-07/2020-08/2020-09 — Re Sean Ozbalt and Re Erin Barr v. Pacific Presbytery
disposition_detail: 2020-07 complaint sustained; censure of deposition annulled. The SJC held Pacific Presbytery clearly erred in handling TE Rankin Wilbourne's BCO 38-1 confession because the Judicial Commission read a six-page report containing new prejudicial assertions beyond the agreed statement of facts. It also held BCO 34-7 was inapplicable because no trial was pending, and that Presbytery erred by ignoring repentance. The SJC recommended treating the 17-month censure as a sufficient BCO 30-3 definite suspension, restoring Wilbourne to ministerial standing without call, and closing the matter; it did not annul Presbytery's dissolution of his call and did not recommend further censure or trial. Companion Complaints 2020-08 and 2020-09 were sustained and answered by reference.
first_summary: Pacific Presbytery deposed TE Rankin Wilbourne after a BCO 38-1 confession. The SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the deposition because the Judicial Commission read a six-page adverse report that went beyond the agreed statement of facts and violated BCO 38-1. It recommended treating the 17-month suspension as sufficient, restoring him to ministerial standing, and closing the matter.
summary: Pacific Presbytery allowed its Judicial Commission to read a six-page adverse report containing new assertions beyond TE Rankin Wilbourne's agreed BCO 38-1 confession, then ruled his sins "base and flagitious" and deposed him. The SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the deposition, holding BCO 38-1 barred the prejudicial report and BCO 34-7 did not apply without a pending trial. It recommended treating the 17-month censure as sufficient definite suspension, restoring ministerial standing without call, and closing the matter; dissolution of his call was not annulled.

sources.supports: Summary, issue, judgment, reasoning, relief, and companion dispositions.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source lines 1–15, 192, 367–373: combined SJC decision dated July 13, 2021, drafted by RE Howie Donahoe, amended and unanimously approved by the Panel with full SJC amendments; roll call 19-0-0. Case No. 2020-07 is expressly one of the three complaints decided.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 19–23 and 122–142: Wilbourne complained that Pacific Presbytery violated BCO 38-1 by allowing the Judicial Commission's adverse six-page report before/alongside the agreed confession, wrongly applied BCO 34-7's "base and flagitious" standard, ignored repentance, overlooked BCO 32-20, denied reasonable defense/counsel during the BCO 31-2 investigation, and failed BCO 31-5/Matthew 18. The issue asks whether Presbytery clearly erred in the BCO 38-1 case and the prior BCO 31-2 investigation (line 214).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 216–262 and 367–369: SJC answered yes, sustained Case 2020-07, and annulled the deposition. Decisive reason: the JC's six-page report contained significant new and prejudicial assertions beyond the agreed Statement of Facts and Confession, violating BCO 38-1; BCO 34-7 did not apply because no trial was pending; Presbytery erred in ignoring repentance. The SJC recommended treating the 17-month censure as definite suspension under BCO 30-3, restoring Wilbourne to ministerial standing without call, and considering the matter closed; it did not annul dissolution of the call and did not recommend further censure or trial unless Presbytery finds a strong presumption of guilt.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 263–365: additional irregularities addressed included BCO 15-1 commission records being filed rather than presented and received, BCO 34-7's public-scandal focus and inapplicability absent pending trial, BCO 38-1's preference for a single agreed document, the right to counsel during investigation, and the investigative commission's failure to interview the accused until its 28th meeting. The SJC stated it was not ruling deposition unwarranted for the confessed offense (lines 342–343) and did not recommend further censure or an indictment and trial (lines 260–262).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 194 and 292: the Panel circulated SJC decisions in Case 2019-10 Evans v. Arizona and Case 2020-04 Williams v. Chesapeake; the SJC applied Evans' BCO 38-1 principle. Lines 367–368: Complaints in Case Nos. 2020-08 and 2020-09 were sustained and answered by reference to this decision.

source_limits: Source is the combined SJC decision for Cases 2020-07, 2020-08, and 2020-09; the filename/title lead with 2020-09, but the final paragraph expressly sustains 2020-07. No separate 2020-07-only opinion or full Record of the Case is supplied; factual details come from the SJC's summary and reasoning. The accusation letter and six-page JC report are not reproduced, only described.
benchmark_examples: C01: preserve mixed outcomes and refused relief while stating the procedural errors.
C02: legitimate investigation and illegitimate censure can coexist; censure may be annulled without acquitting the confessed offense.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged Presbytery action: use of the JC's adverse report in a BCO 38-1 confession, the base-and-flagitious ruling, and the deposition.
score_reasons.decision: States the sustained complaint, annulled censure, and the recommended relief; also preserves that the call dissolution was not annulled.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the adopted BCO 38-1 violation and the inapplicability of BCO 34-7 absent a pending trial.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Captures the BCO 38-1 rule against introducing adverse material beyond the agreed statement and the unusual remedy converting the censure into a 17-month definite suspension.
score_reasons.fidelity: Distinguishes adopted reasoning from party allegations, recommendations from final relief, and does not treat companion case dispositions as the 2020-07 merits.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only details needed to explain the dispute, result, and distinctive procedural rule.
